cities.base: Old Town / Lipscani, for evening walkability and proximity to the Palace of Parliament
cities.name: Bucharest

cities.base: Old town near Piata Sfatului, working base for Bran, Rasnov, and Peles day trips
cities.name: Brasov

cities.base: Inside or just below the citadel walls, for the medieval-town-at-night effect
cities.name: Sighisoara

places.name: Strada Sforii (Rope Street)
places.note: One of the narrowest streets in Europe, about a meter wide. Genuinely five minutes of novelty, don't go out of your way for it but it's on the walk between the square and the fortifications.

places.name: Tampa Hill Cable Car
places.note: Quick ride up for the rooftop view over the old town and the Hollywood-style Brasov sign. Skip in fog or rain, the view is the entire point.

places.name: Piata Sfatului
places.note: The old council square, ringed by pastel facades. Best at golden hour when the day-trippers have thinned out, worth a slow lap rather than a quick photo stop.

places.name: Arcul de Triumf
places.note: Bucharest's own arch on the north side of the city, fine as a five minute stop from a taxi, not worth a special trip on a one night stay.

places.name: Old Princely Court (Curtea Veche) ruins
places.note: Foundation ruins of Vlad the Impaler's court, small and skeletal, the statue out front is the actual photo op.

places.name: Hanul lui Manuc
places.note: Former caravanserai turned courtyard restaurant, more atmosphere than the food deserves but a decent alternative to Caru cu Bere if that's full.

places.name: Stavropoleos Church
places.note: Tiny Brancovenesc-style church wedged between Lipscani buildings, carved stone facade and a quiet courtyard, easy to miss.

places.name: Herastrau Park (Parcul King Michael I)
places.note: Lakefront loop, useful if flight timing leaves a free afternoon and the old town has already been covered.

places.name: Dimitrie Gusti National Village Museum
places.note: Skip on this itinerary, only one night in Bucharest on each end and the Transylvania villages you'll actually visit make this redundant.

places.name: Romanian Athenaeum
places.note: Domed concert hall, interior frescoes are the draw, check if a rehearsal or matinee lets you in without booking a full ticket.

places.name: Cismigiu Gardens
places.note: Oldest public park in the city, quiet lake loop, decent place to reset after a long flight before doing anything that requires standing in line.

places.name: Revolution Square and Kretzulescu Church
places.note: Small square where the 1989 uprising against Ceausescu turned violent, the balcony he fled from is still there, worth five minutes of context if walking past.

places.name: Caru cu Bere
places.note: Neo-gothic beer hall interior is the reason to go, food is average tourist-Romanian and service is rushed given the volume.

places.name: Palace of Parliament
places.note: Mandatory guided tour, book same day or ahead, bring passport for ID check. The scale is the point, this is the second heaviest building on earth.

places.name: Lipscani Old Town
places.note: Pedestrian grid of restored facades, bars and street noise, good for an easy post-flight walk since there's nothing that requires concentration.

places.name: Lipscani Old Town walk
places.note: A low-key reset walk for landing night, not a destination in itself.

places.name: Caru cu Bere
places.note: Atmosphere over food quality, but the room itself is worth the tourist trap trade-off once.

places.name: Palace of Parliament
places.note: Mandatory guided tour, book same-day or ahead, bring your passport since they check ID.

places.name: Sighisoara Citadel and Clock Tower
places.note: The one town in the loop that's actually pretty rather than just historic, don't treat it as a rest stop.

places.name: Tampa Hill cable car
places.note: Skip if weather's bad, the view isn't worth much in fog.

places.name: Piata Sfatului and Black Church
places.note: This square at golden hour is the best fifteen minutes of the trip, don't rush through it.

places.name: Peles Castle
places.note: Interior only by guided tour, plan for a wait; skip the adjacent Pelisor unless you're a serious castle person.

places.name: Rasnov Fortress
places.note: Less crowded than Bran with better hilltop views, and only 15 minutes away so pair them same day.

places.name: Bran Castle
places.note: A tourist machine with a thin Dracula connection, but the building and the views over the pass earn the crowd.

places.name: Rasnov Old Town Square
places.note: Small, unhurried square below the fortress. Good spot for a coffee before or after the climb up.

places.name: Rasnov Fortress
places.note: Less crowded than Bran, better hilltop views over the town and valley. Fifteen minutes from Bran so easy to pair same day.

places.name: Dracula's Castle Wax Museum
places.note: Skip. A cash grab riding on the castle's name, cheap wax figures and nothing historical.

places.name: Cetatuia Restaurant
places.note: Traditional grill near the fortress base, good option if timing lunch around the Rasnov visit instead of Bran.

places.name: Bran Village Walk
places.note: Quiet residential streets behind the tourist strip, worth a short wander if not rushing to Rasnov.

places.name: Conacul Bran Restaurant
places.note: Straightforward Romanian grill and soups a short walk from the castle car park. Not fancy, does the job between Bran and Rasnov.

places.name: Măgura Bran Viewpoint
places.note: Short drive above Bran to a plateau with wide views of the Bucegi and Piatra Craiului ranges. Skip if pressed for time, this is for an extra half day, not the Bran/Rasnov day.

places.name: Bran Cheese and Produce Stalls
places.note: Roadside stalls near the castle entrance selling local sheep cheese and preserves. Good for a snack, not a meal.

places.name: Rasnov Evangelical Church Ruins
places.note: Roofless chapel inside the fortress walls, included with fortress ticket. Worth the few extra minutes for the setting.

places.name: Poarta Transilvaniei (Transylvania Gate) viewpoint
places.note: Roadside pullout marking the historic pass between Transylvania and Wallachia. Quick photo stop on the drive between Bran and Rasnov, nothing more.

places.name: Bran Castle Souvenir Market
places.note: Stalls at the base of the castle path selling wool, cheese, and Dracula kitsch. Fine for ten minutes, not a destination.

places.name: Bran Castle
places.note: Thin Dracula connection but the building itself and the views over the pass justify the crowds. Go right at opening to beat tour buses.

places.name: Torture Museum (Muzeul de Tortura)
places.note: Skip: a cramped private collection of reproduction torture devices with a loose medieval theme, aimed squarely at the Dracula-tourist crowd rather than anything historically grounded.

places.name: Lower Town walk along Strada Cojocarilor
places.note: Ordinary residential street below the citadel, faded facades, actual daily life rather than souvenir stalls. Good contrast walk if the citadel starts to feel like a stage set.

places.name: Rustic Restaurant, Sighisoara
places.note: Romanian home cooking (ciorba, sarmale, papanasi) on a small terrace inside the walls. Cash preferred, service is slow when a bus tour is in town.

places.name: Casa cu Cerb (House with the Stag)
places.note: One of the citadel's oldest houses, easy to spot by the stag head mounted on the corner. Now a hotel, worth a glance walking past rather than a stop.

places.name: Saxon Cemetery behind the Hill Church
places.note: Overgrown Saxon graveyard just past the Hill Church with views over the tiled roofs. Nobody goes up here, which is exactly why it's a good ten minute detour.

places.name: Piata Cetatii (Citadel Square)
places.note: The main square, ringed by pastel Saxon merchant houses. Best around sunset when the tour buses have left and the outdoor cafe tables fill with locals instead.

places.name: History Museum, Sighisoara (in the Clock Tower complex)
places.note: Same ticket as the Clock Tower, covers Sighisoara's Saxon guild history. Modest but fine for a rainy half hour.

places.name: Vlad Dracul House (Casa Vlad Dracul)
places.note: Building where Vlad the Impaler's father supposedly lived, now a mediocre restaurant with a small exhibit upstairs. The connection is thin and the interior isn't worth much, go for the plaque and photo, not the museum.

places.name: Covered Stairway (Scara Acoperita)
places.note: Wooden roofed staircase from 1642 connecting the lower town to the Hill Church, built so schoolchildren could climb in bad weather. Quiet even when the main square isn't.

places.name: Sighisoara Citadel walls and towers
places.note: Nine surviving guild towers (Tinsmiths, Shoemakers, Tailors, Furriers among them) still standing along the fortification walls. Free to walk, uneven cobbles, worth doing before the day-trippers arrive from Brasov.

places.name: Sighisoara Clock Tower (Turnul cu Ceas)
places.note: History museum inside the tower plus the best rooftop view of the citadel's colored roofs. Narrow stairs, small landings, gets congested with tour groups by mid-morning.

places.name: Brasov Citadel (Cetatuia)
places.note: Small 16th century citadel on a hill north of the center, now a restaurant and lookout. Fewer crowds than Tampa, a reasonable alternative if the cable car line is long.

places.name: Schei Gate and Schei Quarter walk
places.note: Wander from the old gate up into the quieter Schei quarter where the Romanian population lived under Saxon rule. Fewer tourists, a good contrast to the main square crowds.

places.name: Council House / History Museum (Casa Sfatului)
places.note: The building in the middle of the square itself, old town hall turned local history museum. Not essential but gives context to the square and is an easy rainy-day filler.

places.name: La Ceaun
places.note: Good lunch stop right on Piata Sfatului, hearty portions of the same sarmale and polenta repertoire. Fine for a midday break between sightseeing rather than a destination meal.

places.name: Bella Muzica
places.note: Cellar restaurant just off the main square, same register of Romanian comfort food as Sergiana. Cozy for a cold evening, book ahead on weekends.

places.name: Sergiana
places.note: Reliable Romanian classics, bear stew shows up on the menu if you're curious. Sarmale and ciorba both solid, service can be slow when a tour bus lands.

places.name: First Romanian School Museum (Schei)
places.note: Small museum in the Schei quarter where the first Romanian-language schooling happened, with old printing presses and manuscripts. Good rainy-day option, quiet even in high season.

places.name: Catherine's Gate (Poarta Ecaterinei)
places.note: Sole surviving medieval city gate, 1559, with the four corner turrets that signaled the town's right to pass its own death sentences. Small but a good stop on a walk of the old fortification line.

outings.why: Two hilltop sites 15 minutes apart, Bran for the crowds and the pass views, Rasnov for a quieter fortress with better views; doable together but it eats the whole day.
outings.name: Bran Castle and Rasnov Fortress
outings.season: year-round, mountain roads can be bad in winter
outings.fallback: If weather's bad, prioritize Rasnov over Bran since the view is the point of both.

outings.why: The interior is only seen by guided tour and you plan for a wait to get on one; skip the adjacent Pelisor unless castles are the whole trip for you.
outings.name: Peles Castle day trip to Sinaia
outings.season: year-round except Mondays (closed), sometimes closes on shor
outings.fallback: Walk the Sinaia monastery grounds nearby if the castle tour queue is too long.

outings.why: The square at golden hour is the best fifteen minutes of the trip; the cable car is only worth it in clear weather.
outings.name: Brasov old town morning: Piata Sfatului, Black Church, Tampa Hill cable car
outings.fallback: Skip the cable car in fog or rain, the view isn't worth much.

outings.why: The one town in the loop that's pretty rather than just historic, worth a slow half day rather than a rushed stop.
outings.name: Sighisoara Citadel and Clock Tower
outings.fallback: None needed, the citadel works in any weather.

destination.name: Romania
destination.pitch: A compact Transylvania loop of castles, fortresses, and one real walled medieval town, strung together on short drives with Bucharest bookending the trip.
destination.caveat: The days are structured around 5-9 hour round-trip outings including driving, so this is a driving-and-castles trip, not a relaxation trip. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Brasov's Piata Sfatului at golden hour and Sighisoara's citadel are the two spots worth lingering in.
because.food: Solid, unfussy Romanian classics like sarmale and ciorba in Brasov, not a food destination in itself.
because.culture: Bran, Rasnov, Peles, and Sighisoara give a real spine of medieval and royal history within two hours of each other.
because.exploration: Sleeping inside Sighisoara's walls beats day-tripping through it.
